title: CGT method statement and all CGT events (Div 102 + Div 104)
summary: The Div 102 method statement (s 102-5) computes the net capital gain: Step 1 reduce capital gains by current-year capital losses, Step 2 apply prior-year net capital losses (or disregard if bankrupt per s 102-5(2)-(3)), Step 3 apply CGT discount percentage (Div 115), Step 4 apply small business concessions (Subdiv 152-C/D/E), Step 5 sum remaining = net capital gain. Div 104 defines all CGT events A1-L8 including K8 (the s 104-5 table is the authoritative completeness list): disposals (A1), use and enjoyment (B1), loss/destruction and endings (C1-C3), rights creation (D1-D4), trusts (E1-E10), leases (F1-F5), shares (G1/G3), special receipts (H1-H2), residency ends (I1-I2), roll-over recapture (J1-J6), special events (K1-K12) and consolidation (L1-L8). Subsection coverage: s 102-5 steps 1-5 mapped; all events from the s 104-5 table mapped; s 102-5(2)-(3) bankruptcy disregard captured as decision node; s 104-5 subsection detail per event (time, gain formula) carried in node bodies; Div 115 discount percentage and Div 112 modifications are separate maps.

nodes.label: A CGT event happens to you (or you are otherwise within Div 102)
nodes.body: Part 3-1 of ITAA 1997 taxes net capital gains. The method statement in s 102-5: work out your capital gains and capital losses for the income year from each CGT event, apply the CGT discount to eligible gains, reduce gains by losses (current year then prior years), and the net capital gain is included in assessable income. Capital losses cannot be deducted from other income — only against capital gains.

nodes.label: Which CGT event applies?

nodes.label: Capital gain worked out — assessable after discount and loss offset
nodes.body: The gain enters the s 102-5 method statement: first reduce by current-year losses, then prior-year losses, then apply discount (if eligible), then small business concessions, and the net capital gain is included in assessable income.

nodes.label: Capital loss — carried forward (can only offset capital gains)
nodes.body: A capital loss cannot be deducted from ordinary income. It reduces current-year capital gains first; any excess is carried forward to future years (s 102-15).

nodes.label: CGT position determined for this event
STEP 1 — Reduce capital gains by current-year capital losses
nodes.body: Reduce the capital gains you made during the income year by the capital losses (if any) you made during the same income year. You choose the order in which you reduce your capital gains. If capital losses exceed capital gains, you have a net capital loss for the year (see s 102-10).

nodes.label: Has the taxpayer become bankrupt or been released from debts under a law relating to bankruptcy?
nodes.body: Under s 102-5(2), if during the income year you became bankrupt or were released from debts under a law relating to bankruptcy, prior-year net capital losses must be disregarded in working out your net capital gain. This applies even if the bankruptcy is annulled under s 74 of the Bankruptcy Act 1966 (s 102-5(3)).

statute.title: Method statement — s 102-5(2)-(3)

nodes.label: STEP 2 — Apply prior-year net capital losses
nodes.body: Apply any previously unapplied net capital losses from earlier income years to reduce the amounts remaining after step 1. Net capital losses are applied in the order in which they were made (oldest first). See s 102-15 for how to apply net capital losses.

nodes.label: STEP 4 — Apply small business concessions (Subdivisions 152-C, 152-D, 152-E)
nodes.body: If any capital gains qualify for the small business concessions, apply them as provided for in Subdivisions 152-C (small business 50% reduction), 152-D (small business retirement exemption) and 152-E (small business roll-over). The basic conditions are in Subdivision 152-A. Note: Subdivision 152-C does not apply to CGT events J2, J5 and J6. Subdivision 152-E does not apply to CGT events J5 and J6.

nodes.label: CGT event K8 — Direct value shifts
nodes.body: A direct value shift occurs affecting your equity or loan interests in a company or trust. Time is when the taxing event generating a gain occurs under s 725-245. Gain = amount of the down interest. [s 104-250].
